H1.name: Visibility of System Status
H1.explanation: Does the system provide immediate and clear feedback about actions and ongoing processes?

H2.name: Match between System and Real World
H2.explanation: Does the interface use familiar language and concepts for users, avoiding technical jargon?

H3.name: User Control and Freedom
H3.explanation: Can users easily undo or exit unwanted actions (e.g., cancel, back, undo)?

H4.name: Consistency and Standards
H4.explanation: Are design elements and terminology consistent throughout the application? Are platform or industry standards followed?

H5.name: Error Prevention
H5.explanation: Are common user errors prevented by the design (e.g., confirmation dialogs, input constraints)?

H6.name: Recognition Rather than Recall
H6.explanation: Are options, instructions, and actions visible rather than requiring users to remember them?

H7.name: Flexibility and Efficiency of Use
H7.explanation: Are there shortcuts or advanced features available for experienced users? Is the interface still simple for novices?

H8.name: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
H8.explanation: Is the interface clean, with only relevant information presented?

H9.name: Help Recognize, Diagnose, Recover from Errors
H9.explanation: Are error messages in plain language, clearly describing the issue and suggesting solutions?

H10.name: Help and Documentation
H10.explanation: Is help or documentation available if needed, even if the interface is mostly self-explanatory?
